messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I'm trying to obtain the matrix of Procrusted Distances among a set of 18 populations. Untill this week everything works fine, but yesterday, running the same script, with the same dataset as before I got an error when running advanced.procD.lm:

fit.pop <- advanced.procD.lm(shape ~ 1,
                         shape ~ pop,
                         groups = ~ pop,
                         iter = 999, data=saldf)

Error: It was not possible to find model terms in the global environment or the data frame used.

However, this model works fine:

fit.pop <- advanced.procD.lm(shape ~ sex,
                         shape ~ sex*pop,
                         groups = ~ pop,
                         iter = 999, data=saldf)

I also performed individual Procrustes ANOVAS por shape, pop, and checked the dataframe. In addition, as I was working with the GitHub Stable version of geomorph, I tried with both, the Develop version and the CRAN one.

Could anyone help me with this problem please?

Thanks in advance,

Lucía

Dear Lucia,

I apologize for the inconvenience. I am in the process of making some updates to RRPP and have made some changes on Github. Because advanced.procD.lm depends on RRPP, there are some cascading effects that I am currently sorting out.

In the interim, you might try installing both geomorph and RRPP from CRAN. Also, be aware that advanced.procD.lm and some other functions will be deprecated in preference to better alternatives. These updates should occur within the next couple of weeks. I only mention this because advanced.procD.lm has proven inflexible to updates of other functions and needs to be retired. Thus, we will not seek to fix emergent issues, as you are now experiencing.

Finally, before trying anything you might try reinstalling RRPP from GitHub first, later today, as I will push some new updates there in the next hour, as we prepare that package for a CRAN submission.

Again, sorry for this inconvenience. You just caught use in a remodeling phase.

Best,
Mike

Hi Alicia,

The problem arises from trying to assign names to specimens in a set when there really is no set - just one specimen.   In this case, the data are no longer formatted as an array.  Furthermore, I’m not sure what will happen when one asks to take the mean of one specimen.  We don’t always anticipate these instances because it takes an awkward case to suggest such cases could exist (who would write a function to find the mean of one observation, normally?).

Whether the problem can be solved depends on what you mean by the problem.  Is there an analytical solution?  Sure.  One could figure that out.  Do you mean can we fix the functions to allow sets of 1 or find the mean of one observation?  This is also possible, but I have to warn you that it cannot supersede the updates we are currently making, but possibly become part of them.  Because we are updating functions for the next geomoprh version, we need to also consider how other updates affect multiple functions, so introducing an additional variable will cause some programming issues.  Maybe in a week or two we might be able to consider this, and only if there is a general solution.  (Sometimes peculiar data sets call for unique solutions rather than general ones.  If a solution is not a geomorph issue, but more of an R issue - like changing arrays to matrices or vectors, inherently, then there might be little we can do avoid pitfalls with geomorph and a kluge might be needed for your data.)

Cheers!
Mike

messages.subject_clean: An error when sliding surface semilandmarks
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am doing a pilot study about putting surface semilandmarks on a group of hominin and modern human skulls (14 hominin and 28 modern humans). The number of surface semilandmarks is 775, which is a lot. I acquired semilandmarks using the Landmark Editor and chose curve semilandmarks using the Geomorph package.

I encountered a problem when I tried to test the intraobserver error as well as the influence of the scan quality. To test these factors, I re-generated semilandmarks from the scan of a specimen, which has been further repaired by the 'Meshdoc' function (for removing small holes and tunnels, etc.) in the Geomagic Studio 14. The regenerated semilandmarks acquired from the repaired scan should be nearly the same as the original semilandmarks. This is because after using the 'gpagen' function without sliding semilandmarks and running the 'plotRefToTarget' function, the thin-plate spline transformation shows nearly no transformation between grids of the original and the re-generated landmark sets.

I then ran the 'gpagen' function with specifying surface and curve sliders. However, an error 'r in La.svd(X, k, k) : error code 1 from Lapack routine 'dgesdd' occurred when the process was 80% done. Interestingly, this error disappears after I replaced the regenerated semilandmark set with the original semilandmark set, though they should be nearly identical.

Does anybody have any idea about this error? I am not sure whether it has anything to do with the small sample size relative to the large number of semilandmarks, since previously the 'gpagen' function runs well with only 6 or 7 specimens.

Thank you very much for taking time to look at my question!

Best regards,
Charles Zhang

This error occurs because the SVD operation in Lapack fails to converge. (for context, Lapack contains the underlying set of Fortran code that R calls for many linear algebra operations, and is rather beyond the control of the R-package programmer).

There are many reasons why this issue could occur, and there are some interesting discussions related to the same error for other packages that use Lapack (e.g., vegan).  In your case, you mentioned that the issue only occurs with the regenerated dataset and not the original. Thus, the issue is in that second dataset.

messages.subject_clean: A question about the result of ProcD.lm
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I tried to repeat the example given in the A Practical Companion to Geometric Morphometrics for Biologists in order to practice using Procrustes ANOVA to test differences between the group means. The example I did was the use of the "apes" data in the "shapes" package. The code is from Chapter 8 statistics

data("apes")
#There is something wrong with specimen #60 so we'll leave it out
apes.dat <- apes$x[,,-60]
apes.proc <- gpagen(apes.dat)
apes.shape <- apes.proc$coords
apes.species <- as.factor(c(rep("gor",59),rep("chimp",53),rep("orang",54)))  #59 gorilla, 53 chimpanzees, 54 orangutans
anova.apes <- procD.lm(apes.shape~apes.species, iter = 999)
anova.apes

The result is an ANOVA table:
                        Df        SS          MS             Rsq          F             Z             Pr(>F)
apes.species   2       0.47304    0.23652     0.46273    70.193    8.4029     0.001 **
Residuals        163   0.54924    0.00337     0.53727
Total                165   1.02228
---
Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

I thought that the p-value should be relatively constant regardless of the number of permutations. However, when I changed the permutation number from 999 to 9999, only the p-value decreases by 10 folds as 0.0001 while the mean square and F value remains constant. Is it because the F test statistic is too large relative to the random sampling F values?

Thank you very much for looking at my question!

Best regards,
Charles Zhang

Charles,

1/1000 = 0.001
1/10000 = 0.0001

P.values are estimates of the true probability of a type I error (finding the observed result in a distribution of all possible random results), which if estimated by a resampling procedure, is constrained by the number of permutations.  It will be rather constant, given a sufficient number of permutations, if the observed result is not extreme (at the tail of the distribution).  For example, a P-value of 0.35 should scale to approximately 0.350, 0.3500, etc.  In your case, 0.001 means none of the 999 random permutations exceeded the observed case; 0.0001 means none of the 9999 random permutations exceeded the observed case.

Mike

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am using the procD.pgls function to test for an association between procrustes aligned skull landmark data of snake skulls of various species and several ecological variables. My independent variables include habitat use (categorical), and proportions of prey types consumed i.e. (propAmbibians, propAnnelids, propFishes, etc.). I am successfully running the PGLS analyses, however, I noticed that the order of the independent variables in the formula affects the p-values.

For example:

procD.pgls(shape ~ Habitat_Use+propAmphibians+propAnnelids, phy=phy, data=Figueroa_notroph)

obtains different p-value estimates for each variable than:

procD.pgls(shape ~ propAnnelids+Habitat_Use+propAmphibians, phy=phy, data=Figueroa_notroph)

I am not changing seed value or permutations (left at default). I had thought that order of main effects did not matter in a PGLS analysis, is there any reason why I may be getting these results with procD.pgls?

Thanks in advance,
Greg

messages.body_plain:
Juan,

I have run a quick example, and results that should be the same in c(BA) vs c(AB) are in fact the same.  Specifically, the rate ratio remains the same, as do the individual rates for each subset (though they of course are reversed).

Significance levels should vary slightly, as they are based on permuting either dataset ‘A’ or dataset ‘B’.

Example code showing the equivalency between c(AB) and c(BA) is below.

Dean

###

library(geomorph)

data(plethspecies)

Y.gpa<-gpagen(plethspecies$land)

A <- two.d.array(Y.gpa$coords)

A1 <- A[,1:10];A2 <- A[,-(1:10)]

gp<-c(rep(1,10),rep(2,12))

gp2<-c(rep(1,12),rep(2,10))

EMR<-compare.multi.evol.rates(A=cbind(A1,A2),gp=gp, Subset=TRUE, phy= plethspecies$phy,iter=999)

EMR2<-compare.multi.evol.rates(A=cbind(A2,A1),gp=gp2, Subset=TRUE, phy= plethspecies$phy,iter=999)

summary(EMR)

summary(EMR2)

EMR3<-compare.multi.evol.rates(A=cbind(A1,A2),gp=gp, Subset=FALSE, phy= plethspecies$phy,iter=999)

EMR4<-compare.multi.evol.rates(A=cbind(A2,A1),gp=gp2, Subset=FALSE, phy= plethspecies$phy,iter=999)

summary(EMR3)

summary(EMR4)
